examination: Civil Services Mains Examination - Optional Subject
provenance_note: Unit text is the published UPSC syllabus for Anthropology Paper I, corroborated across independent reproductions. NOT diffed against the notification PDF. Verify before promoting any mention to verified.
structure_note: Anthropology numbers its syllabus as 1.1/1.2/... with no lettered parts, so section_ref is omitted (rev2 M10 - the question paper's Section A/B cut is a property of the paper, not the syllabus). UPSC's own numbering is preserved at the head of each macro_topic so a reader can map a topic back to the notification.
paper_title_note: paper_title MUST equal subjects.name for slug upsc-cse-mains-opt-anthropology-p1 exactly.

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 1.1-1.3 Meaning, scope and branches of Anthropology
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1.1 Meaning, scope and development of Anthropology. 1.2 Relationships with other disciplines: Social Sciences, Behavioural Sciences, Life Sciences, Medical Sciences, Earth Sciences and Humanities. 1.3 Main branches of Anthropology, their scope and relevance: Social-cultural Anthropology, Biological Anthropology, Archaeological Anthropology, Linguistic Anthropology.
micro_themes: Meaning, scope and development of Anthropology
Relationship with the social, behavioural and life sciences
Relationship with medical sciences, earth sciences and the humanities
Social-cultural Anthropology: scope and relevance
Biological Anthropology: scope and relevance
Archaeological Anthropology: scope and relevance
Linguistic Anthropology: scope and relevance

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 1.4 Human evolution and the emergence of Man
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1.4 Human Evolution and emergence of Man: Biological and Cultural factors in human evolution; Theories of Organic Evolution (Pre-Darwinian, Darwinian and Post-Darwinian); Synthetic theory of evolution; brief outline of terms and concepts of evolutionary biology (Doll's rule, Cope's rule, Gause's rule, parallelism, convergence, adaptive radiation, mosaic evolution).
micro_themes: Biological and cultural factors in human evolution
Pre-Darwinian theories of organic evolution
Darwinian and post-Darwinian theories of organic evolution
Synthetic theory of evolution
Concepts of evolutionary biology: Doll's rule, Cope's rule, Gause's rule
Parallelism, convergence, adaptive radiation and mosaic evolution

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1.5 Characteristics of Primates; Evolutionary Trend and Primate Taxonomy; Primate Adaptations (Arboreal and Terrestrial); Primate Behaviour; Tertiary and Quaternary fossil primates; Living Major Primates; Comparative Anatomy of Man and Apes; Skeletal changes due to erect posture and its implications.
micro_themes: Characteristics of primates and primate taxonomy
Evolutionary trends among primates
Primate adaptations: arboreal and terrestrial
Primate behaviour
Tertiary and Quaternary fossil primates
Living major primates
Comparative anatomy of man and apes
Skeletal changes due to erect posture and their implications

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1.6 Phylogenetic status, characteristics and geographical distribution of: Plio-Pleistocene hominids in South and East Africa (Australopithecines); Homo erectus - Africa (Paranthropus), Europe (Homo erectus heidelbergensis), Asia (Homo erectus javanicus, Homo erectus pekinensis); Neanderthal Man - La-Chapelle-aux-Saints (Classical type), Mt. Carmel (Progressive type); Rhodesian man; Homo sapiens - Cromagnon, Grimaldi and Chancelade.
micro_themes: Plio-Pleistocene hominids of South and East Africa: Australopithecines
Homo erectus in Africa, Europe and Asia
Neanderthal Man: classical and progressive types
Rhodesian man
Homo sapiens: Cromagnon, Grimaldi and Chancelade

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1.7 The biological basis of life: The Cell, DNA structure and replication, Protein Synthesis, Gene, Mutation, Chromosomes, and Cell Division.
micro_themes: The cell; DNA structure and replication
Protein synthesis and the gene
Mutation
Chromosomes and cell division

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1.8 Principles of Prehistoric Archaeology. Chronology: Relative and Absolute Dating methods. 1.9 Cultural Evolution - Broad Outlines of Prehistoric cultures: Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, Neolithic, Chalcolithic, Copper-Bronze age, Iron Age.
micro_themes: Principles of prehistoric archaeology
Relative dating methods
Absolute dating methods
Palaeolithic and Mesolithic cultures
Neolithic and Chalcolithic cultures
Copper-Bronze age and Iron Age

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 2.1-2.2 The nature of culture and society
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 2.1 The Nature of Culture: The concept and characteristics of culture and civilization; Ethnocentrism vis-a-vis cultural Relativism. 2.2 The Nature of Society: Concept of Society; Society and Culture; Social Institutions; Social groups; and Social stratification.
micro_themes: Concept and characteristics of culture and civilization
Ethnocentrism and cultural relativism
Concept of society; society and culture
Social institutions and social groups
Social stratification

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 2.3 Marriage: Definition and universality; Laws of marriage (endogamy, exogamy, hypergamy, hypogamy, incest taboo); Types of marriage (monogamy, polygamy, polyandry, group marriage); Functions of marriage; Marriage regulations (preferential, prescriptive and proscriptive); Marriage payments (bride wealth and dowry).
micro_themes: Definition and universality of marriage
Laws of marriage: endogamy, exogamy, hypergamy, hypogamy, incest taboo
Types of marriage: monogamy, polygamy, polyandry, group marriage
Functions of marriage
Marriage regulations: preferential, prescriptive and proscriptive
Marriage payments: bride wealth and dowry

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 2.4 Family: Definition and universality; Family, household and domestic groups; functions of family; Types of family (from the perspectives of structure, blood relation, marriage, residence and succession); Impact of urbanization, industrialization and feminist movements on family.
micro_themes: Definition and universality of the family
Family, household and domestic groups
Functions of the family
Types of family by structure, blood relation, marriage, residence and succession
Impact of urbanization, industrialization and feminist movements on the family

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 2.5 Kinship: Consanguinity and Affinity; Principles and types of descent (Unilineal, Double, Bilateral, Ambilineal); Forms of descent groups (lineage, clan, phratry, moiety and kindred); Kinship terminology (descriptive and classificatory); Descent, Filiation and Complementary Filiation; Descent and Alliance.
micro_themes: Consanguinity and affinity
Principles and types of descent: unilineal, double, bilateral, ambilineal
Forms of descent groups: lineage, clan, phratry, moiety, kindred
Kinship terminology: descriptive and classificatory
Descent, filiation and complementary filiation
Descent and alliance theory

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 3. Economic organization: Meaning, scope and relevance of economic anthropology; Formalist and Substantivist debate; Principles governing production, distribution and exchange (reciprocity, redistribution and market) in communities subsisting on hunting and gathering, fishing, swiddening, pastoralism, horticulture and agriculture; globalization and indigenous economic systems.
micro_themes: Meaning, scope and relevance of economic anthropology
The formalist and substantivist debate
Reciprocity, redistribution and market exchange
Economies of hunting-gathering, fishing and swiddening communities
Economies of pastoral, horticultural and agricultural communities
Globalization and indigenous economic systems

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 4. Political organization and Social Control: Band, tribe, chiefdom, kingdom and state; concepts of power, authority and legitimacy; social control, law and justice in simple societies.
micro_themes: Band, tribe, chiefdom, kingdom and state
Concepts of power, authority and legitimacy
Social control, law and justice in simple societies

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 5. Religion: Anthropological approaches to the study of religion (evolutionary, psychological and functional); monism, polytheism and monotheism; sacred and profane; myths and rituals; forms of religion in tribal and peasant societies (animism, animatism, fetishism, naturism and totemism); religion, magic and science distinguished; magico-religious functionaries (priest, shaman, medicine man, sorcerer and witch).
micro_themes: Evolutionary, psychological and functional approaches to religion
Monism, polytheism and monotheism
The sacred and the profane; myths and rituals
Animism, animatism, fetishism, naturism and totemism
Religion, magic and science distinguished
Magico-religious functionaries: priest, shaman, medicine man, sorcerer, witch

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 6. Anthropological theories: Classical evolutionism (Tylor, Morgan, Frazer); Historical particularism (Boas); Diffusionism (British, German and American); Functionalism (Malinowski); Structural-functionalism (Radcliffe-Brown); Structuralism (Levi-Strauss, E. Leach); Culture and personality (Benedict, Mead, Linton, Kardiner, Cora du Bois); Neo-evolutionism (Childe, White, Steward, Sahlins, Service); Cultural materialism (Harris); Symbolic and interpretive theories (Turner, Schneider, Geertz); Cognitive theories (Tyler, Conklin); Post-modernism in anthropology.
micro_themes: Classical evolutionism: Tylor, Morgan, Frazer
Historical particularism: Boas
Diffusionism: British, German and American schools
Functionalism: Malinowski
Structural-functionalism: Radcliffe-Brown
Structuralism: Levi-Strauss and E. Leach
Culture and personality: Benedict, Mead, Linton, Kardiner, Cora du Bois
Neo-evolutionism: Childe, White, Steward, Sahlins, Service
Cultural materialism: Harris
Symbolic and interpretive theories: Turner, Schneider, Geertz
Cognitive theories: Tyler, Conklin
Post-modernism in anthropology

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 7. Culture, language and communication: Nature, origin and characteristics of language; verbal and non-verbal communication; social context of language use.
micro_themes: Nature, origin and characteristics of language
Verbal and non-verbal communication
Social context of language use

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 8. Research methods in anthropology: Fieldwork tradition in anthropology; Distinction between technique, method and methodology; Tools of data collection - observation, interview, schedules, questionnaire, case study, genealogy, life-history, oral history, secondary sources of information, participatory methods; Analysis, interpretation and presentation of data.
micro_themes: The fieldwork tradition in anthropology
Technique, method and methodology distinguished
Observation, interview, schedules and questionnaires
Case study, genealogy, life-history and oral history
Secondary sources and participatory methods
Analysis, interpretation and presentation of data

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 9.1 Human Genetics - Methods and Application: family study (pedigree analysis, twin study, foster child, co-twin method, cytogenetic method, chromosomal and karyotype analysis), biochemical methods, immunological methods, DNA technology and recombinant technologies. 9.2 Mendelian genetics in man - family study, single factor, multifactor, lethal, sub-lethal and polygenic inheritance. 9.3 Concept of genetic polymorphism and selection, Mendelian population, Hardy-Weinberg law; mutation, isolation, migration, selection, inbreeding and genetic drift; consanguineous and non-consanguineous mating, genetic load, genetic effect of consanguineous and cousin marriages.
micro_themes: Pedigree analysis, twin study, foster child and co-twin methods
Cytogenetic, chromosomal and karyotype analysis
Biochemical and immunological methods; DNA and recombinant technologies
Mendelian genetics in man: single factor and multifactor inheritance
Lethal, sub-lethal and polygenic inheritance
Genetic polymorphism, selection and the Mendelian population
Hardy-Weinberg law
Mutation, isolation, migration, selection, inbreeding and genetic drift
Consanguineous mating, genetic load and the effects of cousin marriage

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 10 Concept of human growth and development
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 10. Concept of human growth and development: stages of growth - pre-natal, natal, infant, childhood, adolescence, maturity, senescence; Factors affecting growth and development - genetic, environmental, biochemical, nutritional, cultural and socio-economic; Ageing and senescence; Theories and observations - biological and chronological longevity; Human physique and somatotypes; Methodologies for growth studies.
micro_themes: Stages of growth: pre-natal, natal, infant, childhood, adolescence, maturity, senescence
Genetic, environmental and biochemical factors affecting growth
Nutritional, cultural and socio-economic factors affecting growth
Ageing and senescence; biological and chronological longevity
Human physique and somatotypes
Methodologies for growth studies

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 11. Relevance of menarche, menopause and other bio-events to fertility; Fertility patterns and differentials. 12. Demographic theories - biological, social and cultural. 13. Epidemiological Anthropology: Health and disease; Infectious and non-infectious diseases; Nutritional deficiency related diseases.
micro_themes: Menarche, menopause and other bio-events in relation to fertility
Fertility patterns and differentials
Demographic theories: biological, social and cultural
Epidemiological anthropology: health and disease
Infectious and non-infectious diseases
Nutritional deficiency related diseases

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 14. Concept of human adaptation and applications of anthropology: Applied and action anthropology; Anthropology of sports; Nutritional anthropology; Anthropology in designing of defence and other equipments; Forensic Anthropology; Methods and principles of personal identification and reconstruction; Applied human genetics - paternity diagnosis, genetic counselling and eugenics, DNA technology in diseases and medicine, serogenetics and cytogenetics in reproductive biology.
micro_themes: Applied and action anthropology
Anthropology of sports and nutritional anthropology
Anthropology in the design of defence and other equipment
Forensic anthropology: personal identification and reconstruction
Applied human genetics: paternity diagnosis, genetic counselling and eugenics
DNA technology in disease and medicine
Serogenetics and cytogenetics in reproductive biology
